newsitem.title: INDIA: India's SBI staff plan nationwide strike.
newsitem.headline: India's SBI staff plan nationwide strike.

text.p: An association of officers in India's largest bank, State Bank of India (SBI), on Monday threatened to extend its four-day strike to the whole country from June 23.

The All-India SBI Officers' Federation are protesting the suspension of three officers accused by the management of not following procedures in handling the account of CRB Capital Markets, a non-banking finance company that failed last month.
The SBI's operations in Bombay have been affected by the stir, with the head office being paralysed, officials said.
CRB Capital Markets is facing liquidation proceedings.
Representatives of SBI's officers' association met bank chairman M.S. Verma for over two hours on Friday but the two sides failed to reach an amicable settlement.
The strike has affected SBI's money market operations in Bombay but foreign exchange operations, run from Calcutta, are unaffected.
The call money market did not feel the absence of SBI, a major lender, because of abundant liquidity, dealers said.
Call rates were hovering between 2.5 to 3.0 percent on Monday afternoon compared to the opening level of 4.5-5.0 percent, they said.

They said an estimated 20 billion rupees which SBI usually deploys in the call and repo market was now idle because of the strike. At the last repo auction, the Reserve Bank of India collected only 9.0 billion rupees largely because of SBI's absence, dealers said.
SBI's absence is expected to affect a three day repo on Monday evening, they said.
